meta.title: Iran Missile & Drone Tracker
meta.methodology: UAE MoD figures are official cumulative intercepts (highest confidence). Other Gulf state figures are working estimates from official MoD reports, ISW, and Wikipedia cross-referencing. Best-estimate totals include underreporting adjustments for Israel theater and other targets. Launcher estimates derived from IDF/ISW structured reporting. Pre-war stockpile estimates from Atlantic, NYT, IDF, and former US/Israeli officials.
caveats: Pre-Mar 19 data uses a different methodology (less structured, wider ranges)
Kuwait and Qatar cumulatives were significantly revised upward on Mar 23 after Wikipedia cross-reference
Saudi data is methodologically noisy; BM/CM split only available from Mar 20
Drone pre-war estimates range 30K-80K — extremely wide uncertainty
Launcher estimates are judgmental, combining hardware kills with C2/morale degradation
Production was ongoing early in the war but is assessed as halted for BMs since ~Mar 29
Cease-fire extended indefinitely Apr 22 at Pakistan's request; all figures frozen pending resumption or permanent deal
ISW Apr 19 / US officials to NYT: Iran dug ~100 launchers from underground storage during ceasefire; effective launcher count revised from ~102 to ~200 as of Apr 23
FDD/Long War Journal Apr 19: Kuwait revised to 369 BMs + 852 drones; Saudi revised to 68 BMs + 612 drones — Kuwait drone figure is ~30% higher than prior tracking estimate

Conditional liveness of this tracker holds at ~23% (Rule B's P(rupture-scenario)). The first 48 hours of the post-revision regime have produced no observable that would re-open Rule C / Rule A optionality; the comparator ladders remain published through the May 28 reconvergence horizon.

CEASE-FIRE Day 50 — launcher count stable at ~200 (reconstitution plateau Day 34; 38 days since the ISW Apr 19 anchor). Fire-silence Day 46 — third full calendar day on the asymmetric side of the pre-silence-duration boundary (46 > 43; 107% of pre-silence duration). 2 IRGC-seized vessels still held near Hormuz (Day 35). 3rd US carrier in theater. BM production still halted. Post-revision Day 3 / T+168h post-cliff / T+72h post-revision — RECONVERGENCE EVE: seven compounded null days since the cliff shift rule posterior weights to ~9/30/61 — Rule B firmly dominant; the May 28 00:00 UTC reconvergence horizon is ~24 hours away, at which point comparator ladders A and C are dropped from the dashboard and Rule B becomes the single live ladder (first dashboard architecture change since the May 20 cliff). Conditional liveness of this tracker holds at ~23% (Rule B's P(rupture-scenario)). The calendar landmarks stack at the 50-day ceasefire mark: ceasefire Day 50, fire-silence Day 46 (107% of pre-silence interval), reconstitution plateau Day 34, anchor-data lag 38/48 days, T+168h (one full week) post-cliff.

keyEvents.text: War begins — Iran launches massive opening salvos
SRBM revelation: pre-war BM stockpile revised to 8K-11K (was 2.5-3K)
BM fire rate down 86% from Day 1; interceptor crisis emerging
BM fire rate down 90%; IRGC naval fleet effectively destroyed
Tracker restructured — methodology shift to floor/best-estimate model
IRGC Aerospace Force Commander killed in Esfahan
IRGC drone unit commander killed — 2nd C2 kill in 48h; IRBMs at Diego Garcia
Kuwait/Qatar cumulatives revised sharply upward after cross-reference
Strait of Hormuz mined; IDF 600+ strikes on BM sites; morale collapse
WaPo: 4 key BM production facilities destroyed; production 'most likely halted'
UAE surge: +60 BMs in 3 days; CM usage accelerating; China fuel chemicals
Iran targeting civilian infrastructure — desalination, refineries, ports
Trump ultimatum on Strait of Hormuz; Al Jubail industrial hub struck
CEASE-FIRE announced — 2-week deal via Pakistan/China mediation; Strait to reopen; BM rate already declining sharply
Post-ceasefire salvos (pipeline delay): Kuwait 28 drones, Qatar 7 BMs + drones, Saudi 9 drones, UAE engaged incoming; Iran-US talks Friday
Bahrain official uplift: 188 BMs / 468 drones (+158 drones — 51% in one update). UAE updated: 537 BMs / 26 CMs / 2,256 drones. Overnight quiet.
CEASE-FIRE Day 3 — holds overnight. Iran-US talks in Islamabad (Phase 1 → 45-day Phase 2 window). Both sides depleted: ~102 launchers remain; Gulf Patriots ~75% spent.
CEASE-FIRE Day 4 — Kuwait National Guard site struck by drones (Apr 10 Thu night); several injured. IRGC denied. Iran threatens Islamabad walkout over Lebanon strikes + Hormuz dispute.
CEASE-FIRE Day 6 — Islamabad Round 1 collapsed; Round 2 being arranged. Israel-Lebanon ceasefire holding. Zero Iran-direct fire since Apr 11.
Reuters: US/Iran scaled back to temporary memorandum — comprehensive deal off table for now. Round 2 talks imminent. Netanyahu supports ceasefire.
Iran FM Araghchi declares Hormuz 'completely open' for commercial vessels. Trump: US blockade 'will remain in full force.' BBC tracking shows few ships actually moving.

CEASE-FIRE Day 12 — holding. Zero fire since Apr 11. ~3 days to Apr 22 expiry. Islamabad Round 2 set for Mon Apr 21. 45-day extension on table. Netanyahu supports ceasefire. 50,000 US personnel in theater.

CEASE-FIRE Day 13 — holding. Islamabad Round 2 underway today. 45-day extension on table; decision expected before Apr 22 expiry. ISW assessment published: Iran retains ~1,000 of 2,500 pre-war MRBMs; 'well under 50%' of drones intact. Hormuz declared open by Iran FM but US blockade remains; Lloyd's List tracking shows minimal transit.

CEASE-FIRE Day 14 (FINAL) — expires 0000 GMT Apr 22. Trump: extension 'highly unlikely.' Iran FM: 'no talks with US for now.' US seized Iranian cargo ship (blockade running); Tehran vowed retaliation. Naval blockade: 9 ships turned back. Fire-silence Day 11. Islamabad Round 2 status: Iran participation uncertain. Both sides signaling toughness in final hours while math shows both deeply depleted.

CEASE-FIRE EXTENDED INDEFINITELY — Trump reversed 'highly unlikely' stance hours before 0000 GMT Apr 22 expiry at Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif's request. US naval blockade remains in full force; military 'ready and able.' VP Vance ME trip on hold. Fire-silence Day 12 (zero Iran-direct launches since Apr 11). Unclaimed attack struck Iran's Lavan Island oil refinery and Sirri Island crude export facilities overnight — first strike on Iranian oil infrastructure during the freeze. War freeze now open-ended; depletion tracker remains paused.

LAUNCHER RECONSTITUTION CONFIRMED — ISW Apr 19 / US officials to NYT: Iran has dug ~100 launchers from underground hardened facilities since the ceasefire began. Effective launcher count revised from ~102 to ~200 (60% of pre-war fleet). Days to BM functional zero from resumption extends from ~51 to ~100 days. US officials: Iran retains ~70% missile stockpile, ~40% drones, ~60% launchers. FDD/LWJ Apr 19: Kuwait theater revised to 369 BMs + 852 drones — 30% more drones than prior tracking estimate. Fire-silence Day 13. No new official Gulf cumulative tallies.

NAVAL PROVOCATION — IRGC Navy seized 2 commercial vessels near Strait of Hormuz Apr 22: first naval action since truce. Islamabad Round 2 postponed indefinitely; Iran's Mohammadi called ceasefire extension a 'ploy to buy time for surprise strike.' Trump announced Israel-Lebanon ceasefire extended 3 weeks (Apr 23). Fire-silence Day 16 — zero Iran-direct launches since Apr 11. All Gulf cumulative totals unchanged. Iran holding reconstituted posture: ~200 launchers, ~70% BMs, ~40% drones.

CEASEFIRE DAY 19 — Fire-silence Day 18. No new Iran-direct launches since Apr 11. 2 IRGC-seized vessels near Hormuz still held (Day 3). Islamabad Round 2: no new date set. Coalition Patriot interceptor resupply window now 19 days old — the asymmetric recovery the fire-silence enables. Iran frozen: ~200 launchers, ~70% BMs, ~40% drones. US blockade in full force. No new Gulf official cumulative tallies.

SPLIT SIGNAL — Direct fire-silence Day 19, but Apr 24 Kuwait struck by 2 Iraq-launched proxy drones (Islamic Resistance in Iraq, no casualties). First kinetic incident since Apr 22 vessel seizures. Trump orders third US carrier to region — signals US intelligence concern over Iran's reconstituted posture. Iran FM Araghchi to Islamabad for consultations; talks deadlocked over Hormuz blockade. 2 IRGC-seized vessels still held. No new official Gulf cumulative tallies.

DAY 20 — Longest fire-silence of the war. No deal reached; Islamabad Round 2 postponed indefinitely; Hormuz blockade unchanged. 2 IRGC-seized vessels still held near Hormuz (Day 5). 3rd US carrier now in theater. Iran posture: ~200 launchers (doubled from ceasefire baseline), ~70% BM stock, ~40% drones. 18 days since last official Gulf cumulative tally. Military balance at Day 20 favors Iran on launchers; coalition on interceptors. Ceasefire intact at direct-Iran level; proxy fringe (Apr 24 Kuwait) and naval coercion continue.

DAY 25 — Fire-silence Day 21. P(Hormuz reopen 30d) = ~15% unchanged; rolling window May 2–Jun 1. 2 IRGC-seized vessels still held near Hormuz (Day 10). No Round 3 date. Chinese mediation not engaged despite direct economic stake as Iran's largest crude buyer; structural obstacles identified. 23 days since last official Gulf cumulative tally. Iran posture stable: ~200 launchers, ~70% BMs, ~40% drones. Coalition Patriot resupply window Day 25. Stalemate self-reinforcing; no forcing function visible.

DAY 35 — Fire-silence Day 31; Iran enters second calendar month of zero direct fire since Apr 11. P(Hormuz reopen 30d) = ~15% unchanged, static for 14 consecutive days; rolling window May 12–Jun 11. 8 days to the methodology's pre-committed May 20 partial-arrangement calendar threshold — beyond it, the 9 pp partial-arrangement contribution to P(reopen) becomes mechanically infeasible to execute within the window. 2 IRGC-seized vessels still held (Day 20). No Round 3 date. Reconstitution plateau Day 19. Anchor-data lag: 23 days since ISW/FDD/LWJ Apr 19; 33 days since UAE Apr 9 cumulative.

DAY 37 — Fire-silence Day 33. P(Hormuz reopen 30d) = ~15% unchanged, static for 16 consecutive days (Apr 28–May 14); rolling window May 14–Jun 13. 6 days to the May 20 partial-arrangement cliff. 2 IRGC-seized vessels still held near Hormuz (Day 22) — past the typical Iranian-seizure demand-articulation window without published quid pro quo. Reconstitution plateau Day 21. Anchor-data lag: 25 days since ISW/FDD/LWJ Apr 19; 35 days since UAE Apr 9 cumulative. The post-cliff scenario-redistribution question is now operational: when the partial-arrangement scenario evicts on May 20, where does its 15 pp of scenario probability mass redistribute — proportionally, into stalemate, or into rupture?

DAY 40 — Fire-silence Day 36. P(Hormuz reopen 30d) = ~15% unchanged, static for 19 consecutive days (Apr 28–May 16); rolling window May 17–Jun 16. 3 days to the May 20 partial-arrangement cliff. 2 IRGC-seized vessels still held near Hormuz (Day 25 since Apr 22). Reconstitution plateau Day 24. Anchor-data lag: 28 days since ISW/FDD/LWJ Apr 19; 38 days since UAE Apr 9 cumulative. Today's pivot is the first post-cliff observable: Rules A/B/C produce identifiably different posteriors over what the May 21–24 signal stream should look like; the first authoritative data drop after the cliff fires is the only window in which the three redistribution rules diverge sharply in their predictions and is therefore a natural experiment against the methodology's pre-committed Rule C choice.

DAY 42 — Fire-silence Day 38. P(Hormuz reopen 30d) = ~15% unchanged, static for 21 consecutive days (Apr 28–May 18); rolling window May 19–Jun 18. 1 day to the May 20 partial-arrangement cliff — eviction fires inside the next 24-hour cycle. 2 IRGC-seized vessels still held near Hormuz (Day 27 since Apr 22). Reconstitution plateau Day 26. Anchor-data lag: 30 days since ISW/FDD/LWJ Apr 19; 40 days since UAE Apr 9 cumulative. Today's pivot is the baseline lock-in window — the three-rule post-cliff ladder is now formally pre-published under timestamp: Rule C (primary, smoothed asymmetric) Stalemate 65% / Rupture 28% / Comprehensive 7% / Partial 0% → P(reopen) ≈ 6.3%; Rule A (proportional) → ~7.4%; Rule B (all-into-stalemate) → ~6.3%. Headline disagreement collapses to ~1.1 pp; the load-bearing disagreement is now entirely in the underlying P(rupture-scenario) band (23%–28%).

DAY 43 — CLIFF FIRED. The May 20 00:00 UTC partial-arrangement scenario eviction triggered on schedule per the calendar-threshold rule; no Round 3 announcement materialized in the 24-hour terminal window (unconditional 1-day joint probability ~1%, credibility-filter-passing ~0.5%). Live ladder is now pre-committed Rule C: Stalemate 65% / Rupture 28% / Comprehensive 7% / Partial 0% → P(reopen) ≈ 6.3% (Rule A comparator ~7.4%, Rule B ~6.3%). Headline dial drops ~8.7 pp from yesterday's 15% in a single mechanical step — largest single-day move since the Hormuz tracker started, and the first move without a coincident external event. Watch list phase-transitioned: four partial-scenario conditioning indicators (Round 3 date, Chinese/Omani mediation, Saudi/UAE partial support, US/Iran back-channel) retire mechanically; post-cliff list collapses to four operative indicators (~75% negative-side by trigger weight). Fire-silence Day 39; 28 days since IRGC seizures; reconstitution plateau Day 27. Tracker A conditional-liveness probability tightens from ~23% to ~28% under the new Rule C posterior.

DAY 44 — T+24h post-cliff. P(Hormuz reopen 30d) = ~6.3% (Rule C, primary) unchanged from yesterday's eviction posterior. The first 24 hours of the May 21–24 natural-experiment window are now closed. Observed signal across the window: zero. The IRGC Naval channel — silent for 29 consecutive days since the Apr 22 vessel seizures — remained silent through the first post-cliff calendar day; no fresh seizure, no release, no new naval incident. No authoritative posture revision from ISW or Gulf MoD (anchor-data lag now 32 days / 42 days respectively). No commercial transit cluster. No rupture indicator. Under the published read-grid, 24 hours of zero-event silence is mild Bayesian evidence in favor of Rule B (all-into-stalemate) over Rule C (asymmetric/rupture-weighted) — the rule-invariant headline of ~6.3% is unchanged, but the composition of the underlying P(rupture-scenario) eases back toward 23–25% from the Rule C posterior of 28%. The natural-experiment window has ~72 hours to run; the IRGC Naval channel remains the single most informative sub-indicator. Rolling window May 21–Jun 20; reconstitution plateau Day 28; fire-silence Day 40.

DAY 45 — T+48h post-cliff. P(Hormuz reopen 30d) = ~6.3% (Rule C, primary) unchanged for the third consecutive day. The May 21–24 natural-experiment window is now at its midpoint (50% elapsed). The second 24-hour calendar day produced the same observed signal as the first: zero. The IRGC Naval channel — silent for 30 consecutive days since the Apr 22 vessel seizures — remained silent through a second full post-cliff calendar day; no fresh seizure, no release, no incident. No authoritative posture revision from ISW or Gulf MoD (anchor-data lag now 33 / 43 days). No commercial-transit cluster. No rupture indicator. The compounded Bayesian update across two null days shifts posterior weights from yesterday's ~28/33/39 to roughly ~24/33/44 — Rule B (all-into-stalemate) is now the modal posterior on the rule weighting for the first time since the cliff fired. Rule C primary is held on theoretical grounds pending the pre-committed 00:00 UTC May 25 methodology-revision threshold, which is now ~48 hours away. The rule-invariant headline holds at ~6.3%; the underlying P(rupture-scenario) eases further from yesterday's ~25% toward ~24% on the weighted posterior; Tracker A conditional liveness softens by another ~1 pp. The remaining ~48 hours decide whether the methodology revises primary from C to B at the threshold, or whether a late naval cluster reverses the compounded update and re-corroborates Rule C. Fire-silence Day 41 (95% of the war's 43-day pre-silence direct-fire interval); reconstitution plateau Day 29; rolling window May 22–Jun 21.

DAY 46 — T+72h post-cliff. P(Hormuz reopen 30d) = ~6.3% (Rule C, primary) unchanged for the fourth consecutive day. The May 21–24 natural-experiment window has now entered its terminal 24-hour quarter (75% elapsed). The third 24-hour calendar day produced the same observed signal as the first two: zero. The IRGC Naval channel — silent for 31 consecutive days since the Apr 22 vessel seizures — remained silent through a third full post-cliff calendar day; no fresh seizure, no release, no incident, no commercial-transit cluster, no rupture indicator. No authoritative posture revision from ISW or Gulf MoD (anchor-data lag now 34 / 44 days). The compounded Bayesian update across three null days shifts posterior weights from yesterday's ~24/33/44 to roughly ~20/32/48 — Rule B (all-into-stalemate) is now within ~2 pp of majority on the rule weighting; Rule C has lost ~40% of its uniform-prior weight in three calendar days; Rule A holds. Rule C primary is held on theoretical grounds pending the pre-committed 00:00 UTC May 25 methodology-revision threshold, which is now ~24 hours away. Rule-weighted P(window closes empty) ~85%, so the mechanical Rule C → Rule B revision is now more likely than not to fire on schedule. A single fresh IRGC vessel seizure inside the next 24 hours still inverts the posterior from ~20/32/48 to ~56/30/14 — the asymmetric optionality is intact but its calendar exposure is nearly consumed. The rule-invariant headline holds at ~6.3%; the underlying P(rupture-scenario) eases further from yesterday's ~24% toward ~23%, converging on Rule B's value; Tracker A conditional liveness softens by another ~1 pp. Fire-silence Day 42 (98% of the war's 43-day pre-silence direct-fire interval; pre-silence-duration boundary crossed tomorrow); reconstitution plateau Day 30; rolling window May 23–Jun 22.

DAY 48 — REVISION FIRED. The mechanical methodology revision from Rule C (smoothed asymmetric) to Rule B (all-into-stalemate) triggered at 00:00 UTC May 25 on schedule, conditional on the observed four-day null window outcome. Live ladder is now Rule B: Stalemate 70% / Rupture 23% / Comprehensive 7% / Partial 0% → P(reopen) ≈ 6.3% (Rule A comparator ~7.4%; Rule C comparator ~6.3% retained through May 28). Headline rule-invariant — dashboard dial does not move. Five published values updated in single discrete step: scenario ladder 65/28/7/0 → 70/23/7/0; P(rupture-scenario) 28% → 23%; Tracker A conditional liveness ~28% → ~23%; primary discriminator language re-framed (IRGC Naval channel from corroboration under Rule C to falsification under Rule B); headline P(reopen) ~6.3% unchanged. Fire-silence Day 44 — for the FIRST TIME the silence is longer than the active-fire phase that preceded it (44 > 43; 102% of pre-silence duration). 2 IRGC-seized vessels still held (Day 33). Reconstitution plateau Day 32. Anchor lag 36 / 46 days. Rule posterior weights at T+120h ~12/31/57 in favor of Rule B.

DAY 49 — Post-revision Day 2 / T+144h post-cliff, T+48h post-revision. P(Hormuz reopen 30d) = ~6.3% (Rule B, primary) unchanged for the seventh consecutive day. The first 48 hours of the post-revision regime produced the same observed signal as the four pre-revision natural-experiment days: zero events across all seven enumerated read-grid channels. The IRGC Naval channel — silent for 34 consecutive days since the Apr 22 vessel seizures — remained silent through both full post-revision calendar days; no fresh seizure, no release, no incident, no commercial-transit cluster, no rupture indicator, no anchor revision, no Round 3 announcement, no proxy escalation cluster. Six compounded null days since the cliff shift rule posterior weights to ~10/30/60 — Rule B is now firmly dominant with ~60% of the remaining hypothesis mass; Rule C reduced to ~10% (the falsifying-event window is structurally closing); Rule A holds at ~30% (the proportional rule is the consistent-with-anything fallback). Anchor-data lag 37 days (ISW/FDD/LWJ Apr 19) / 47 days (UAE Apr 9). The comparator ladders remain published through the May 28 reconvergence horizon, after which they are dropped and Rule B becomes the single live ladder. Conditional liveness of Tracker A holds at Rule B's value of ~23%. Today's pivot is the post-revision steady state: the boring-case forecast from the May 19 baseline-lock-in pre-publication has now carried both endpoints (cliff and revision) without operator discretion; the dashboard dial has not moved across either transition. Fire-silence Day 45 — second full calendar day on the asymmetric side of the pre-silence-duration boundary (45 > 43; 105% of pre-silence duration). Reconstitution plateau Day 33. Rolling window May 26–Jun 25.

DAY 50 — RECONVERGENCE EVE. Post-revision Day 3 / T+168h post-cliff, T+72h post-revision. P(Hormuz reopen 30d) = ~6.3% (Rule B, primary) unchanged for the eighth consecutive day; seventh consecutive null calendar day since the cliff. IRGC Naval channel silent 35 consecutive days since Apr 22 vessel seizures; no fresh seizure, no release, no commercial-transit cluster, no rupture indicator, no anchor revision, no Round 3 announcement, no proxy escalation cluster. Seven compounded null days since the cliff shift rule posterior weights from ~10/30/60 yesterday to ~9/30/61 today — Rule B at ~61% of remaining hypothesis mass; Rule C reduced to ~9% (the falsifying-event window has now structurally consumed nearly its full calendar exposure); Rule A holds at ~30%. Anchor-data lag 38 days (ISW/FDD/LWJ Apr 19) / 48 days (UAE Apr 9). The May 28 00:00 UTC reconvergence horizon is now ~24 hours away — the comparator ladders A and C are dropped from the dashboard per the post-eviction natural-experiment rule and Rule B becomes the single live ladder; this is the first dashboard architecture change since the May 20 cliff. Conditional liveness of Tracker A holds at Rule B's value of ~23%. Fire-silence Day 46 — third full calendar day on the asymmetric side of the pre-silence-duration boundary (46 > 43; 107% of pre-silence duration). Reconstitution plateau Day 34. Rolling window May 27–Jun 26. Today's pivot is the calendar-coincident landmark stack at the 50-day ceasefire mark: Day 50 ceasefire, Day 46 fire-silence (107% of pre-silence interval), reconstitution plateau Day 34, anchor-data lag 38/48 days, T+168h (one full week) post-cliff — all intersecting at a single threshold tomorrow.
